newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Rugby League: Manly, St George to play in ARL grand final.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Rugby League: Manly, St George to play in ARL grand final.

text.p: Manly on Sunday scored four unanswered tries to trounce Cronulla 24-0 in an Australian Rugby League (ARL) premiership semifinal and reach next week's grand final against St George.
St George upset North Sydney 29-12 on Saturday to book an unexpected berth in the grand final.
A methodical Manly lived up to the form which saw them comfortably top the ARL standings at the end of regular season matches and they completely outclassed the young Cronulla side.
The only black note for Manly was a head injury suffered by New Zealand fullback Matthew Ridge early in the match.
Ridge was taken from the field unconscious on a motorised stretcher 25 minutes into the match after attempting a tackle on Cronulla centre Paul Donaghy
Manly medical staff later told reporters Ridge had been badly concussed after being hit in the head by Donaghy's knee.
The fitness of Ridge will now be one of Manly's primary concerns in the leadup to next Sunday's grand final.
Ridge had kicked a penalty goal in the 10th minute and had a hand in his side's first try, scored by veteran standoff Cliff Lyons, as Manly set up a 6-0 halftime lead.

The second half started badly for Cronulla when fullback David Peachey dropped the ball in a tackle in only the first minute, allowing Manly secondrower Steve Menzies to cross for his side's second try.
Another Peachey error 18 minutes later, this time from a high kick by Lyons, led to a try by winger Danny Moore.
Menzies then crossed for his second try six minutes from fulltime to give Manly an unbeatable lead.
St George booked a place in the grand final with a convincing win over North Sydney on Saturday to complete a remarkable resurgence this season.
The Saints scored five tries to two in front of 37,779 fans, an unlikely result after they had been ranked 100-1 outsiders at the start of the year.
St George were left in disarray at the start of the season when coach Rod Reddy and a number of key players left and the club considered a merger because of financial troubles.

But fullback Dean Raper, centre Mark Bell, standoff Anthony Mundine, lock Wayne Bartrim and replacement forward Nathan Brown put those troubled times far behind them by each scoring a try against Norths.
Bartrim added four goals and scrumhalf Noel Goldthorpe kicked a drop goal for the Saints, who led 7-6 at halftime.

After their early internal divisions, St George's revival was orchestrated by coach David Waite, whose side only scraped into the playoffs with a late charge to claim one of the top eight positions in the league at the end of the regular season.
North Sydney, who were favourites to secure their first grand final appearance since 1943, scored tries through fullback Matt Seers and hooker Mark Soden.
Scrumhalf Jason Taylor kicked two goals in a nervous, disappointing team performance.
Manly and St George have played in two previous grand finals, in 1957 and 1959, with St George winning both times.
-- Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
